newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSTANT VIEW - JAPAN JUNE CURRENT ACCOUNT SURPLUS.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - JAPAN JUNE CURRENT ACCOUNT SURPLUS.

text.p: The following is a selection of initial reactions by economists and analysts to Japan's June current account surplus figures, which the Ministry of Finance (MOF) said on Friday rose 55.8 pct to 1.02 trillion yen.
CHRIS PAVLOU, TREASURER GLOBAL MARKETS, MIDLAND BANK TOKYO:
"They look at the top of the expectations. I think it's good news for everybody. Imports have gone up too. So this would take a bit of pressure off the dollar going higher."
RICHARD JERRAM, CHIEF ECONOMIST, ING BARINGS SECURITIES TOKYO:

"Clearly, the surplus is continuing to go up. ...we've already got some indications for July, it looks like we're heading for another big rise there after this rather larger than expected rise in June. We see no end to the rising surplus just because domestic demand is weak. Because of weak domestic demand, import growth is going to be slow and so the surplus is just going to keep on rising for a year, possibly two years."

"We think it's inevitable that trade friction will increase. The main reason for this is Japanese manufacturers are facing very weak demand at home so they've been forced to look to overseas markets to sell their goods. The most high profile example of that is the auto industry, which has seen a very scary inventory buildup in the last few months because they've clearly misjudged how weak domestic demand has become for their products. As a result, they're exporting frantically and provoking quite a reaction from the United States. And I think this is just going to get worse in the coming months."
MINEKO SASAKI-SMITH, CHIEF ECONOMIST, CREDIT SUISSE FIRST BOSTON SECURITIES TOKYO:

"The current figures may be exaggerated due to the effects of the sales tax rise in April, but it will take six to nine months for the effect of the yen's weakening to 127 yen (to a dollar) back in May to disappear. So the surplus will continue to rise gradually."
